merges.why: Both name one mechanism: a reviewer in one committee based a score on a checkable factual claim about the paper or its prior work that was wrong. R01 covers the error that lowered a score and R19 the error that raised one; the sign of the error is the only difference, and either sign opens the same gap between committees.

Both name one mechanism: the authors posted information on one committee's forum only, so the two committees judged different information. R04 covers a disclosed flaw and R35 new results; the content's direction is the only difference.

reasoning: I compared every entry with every other and merged only where the definitions name the same causal mechanism and differ only in its direction. I kept overlapping entries apart when they name different mechanisms: R02 (chair's own reading lifted the tier) and R30 (tier with no stated case); R03 (enthusiastic low-confidence score) and R27 (checked champion); R12 (thin review counted) and R26 (silent detractor discounted); R06 (rebuttal moved scores) and R17 (non-experts persuaded without checks); R07 and R08, and R16 and R18, which their definitions separate explicitly; R15 (held score on the same peripheral point) and R20 (shifted to new grounds); R22 (committee acted on the stated stance) and R25 (committee counted the unexplained raised score); R24 (expertise and clarity) and R31 (expertise and baseline checks); R36 (an expert outweighed by the mean) and R40 (no reviewer could check the core); R33 (narrow audience) and R39 (overstated claim); R13 and R14, which differ in whether the chair's own view was positive.
